title: How to Measure Customer Satisfaction Without Expensive Tools

facts.fact: Adwave's page says a CSAT score can be calculated with a 1 to 10 scale by adding the responses, dividing by the total number of respondents, and turning the result into a percentage-based metric.
facts.quote: You can use a simple **1 to 10 scale**, add the responses, divide by the total number of respondents, and turn that into a percentage-based metric.

facts.fact: CustomerSure, a third-party source cited by Adwave, says businesses should trigger customer satisfaction feedback within 15 minutes of the interaction.
facts.quote: businesses should trigger feedback **within 15 minutes** of the interaction

facts.fact: CustomerSure reports that surveys sent after 24 hours show a 60% drop in recall validity.
facts.quote: surveys sent after **24 hours** show a **60% drop in recall validity**

facts.fact: CustomerSure claims its recommended four-layer framework has a 35% higher correlation with actual revenue growth than single-metric tracking.
facts.quote: It reports this approach has a **35% higher correlation with actual revenue growth** than single-metric tracking.

facts.fact: Feedback Robot states that passive measurement through review velocity and sentiment analysis on Google and Yelp can reach 92% accuracy in predicting churn when tracking a 30-day sentiment shift.
facts.quote: can reach **92% accuracy in predicting churn** when tracking a **30-day sentiment shift**

facts.fact: Feedback Robot warns that businesses focusing only on average rating can miss a 25% higher churn risk when review frequency drops by 40% while sentiment stays stable.
facts.quote: can miss a **25% higher churn risk** when review frequency drops by **40%** while sentiment stays stable.
